newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian stocks slip, seen drifting.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian stocks slip, seen drifting.

text.p: Slovenian shares ended 0.72 percent lower on Wednesday ahead of a long weekend but traders forecast a slightly firmer bias for the coming week.
The bourse will be closed on Thursday and Friday.
"Shares will probably remain at the same level or gain slightly in the week before the elections," Karmen Cerar, a trader at brokerage Poteza said.
Traders said that foreign investors seem to be taking a wait-and-see stance ahead of the general elections scheduled for November 10.
The SBI index fell 8.69 points to 1,192.07. Overall 10 shares fell and seven rose, while seven were untraded.
Turnover fell to 185.9 million tolars from 231.4 million.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded, firming 1.40 percent to an average of 40,273 tolars on volume of 1,803 shares for total turnover of 72.5 million tolars.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, falling 13.59 percent to 42,679 tolars on volume of 545 shares for total turnover of 23.3 million tolars.

The biggest gainer was construction company GPG, firming 3.90 percent to 8,000 tolars on volume of 20 shares for total turnover of 160,000 tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
